title: REGEXTEST escape battery: 18 divergences before the repair, 40/40 after, same cases
upstream_status_verbatim: the working-tree repair expands the admitted escape set locally and is now live-Excel signed off; bead `oxf-fyhi` stays open until checkpoint/landing.
status_plain: A 40-escape REGEXTEST("a1.B z","\X") battery against Excel 16.0 build 20026 found 18 divergences, all of the form "OxFunc rejects what Excel admits" - anchors, whitespace escapes and escaped metacharacters. After the repair the SAME 40-case battery was replayed via COM and scored 40/40 exact typed matches with 0 mismatches on the same build. The corpus is therefore the repair's own fitting set, and the source says so in the same sentence as the figure ("the same 40-case escape battery"). Every case in this battery is a REGEXTEST call. REGEXEXTRACT and REGEXREPLACE are never named in the stream and were not themselves swept; they do share the repaired parse_escape_atom / parse_class_piece parser, but the capture and replacement semantics they add on top are unmeasured, and no OxFunc document inherits the 40/40 onto them.

counts.capture_route: desktop Excel via COM, the same 40-case escape battery

open_question: REGEXEXTRACT and REGEXREPLACE have no Excel comparison. Whether the shared parser repair reaches their capture and replacement semantics is untested.
reader_warning: The 40/40 is REGEXTEST's alone, and it was scored on the same battery the repair was fitted to - so it demonstrates that the fix closed the 18 known divergences, not that the escape set is right on inputs nobody probed. It measures which escapes are admitted and what they match; it says nothing about numeric results. The 24/24 elsewhere in this stream is a cargo test count, not an Excel comparison.
